title: The Merchant and the Two Sharpers

keywords: the merchant and the two sharpers
full_text:
An honest grain merchant was leading a sleek, well-fed donkey laden with two sacks of fine wheat to the central market of Cairo. Walking behind the beast, the merchant held the halter loosely in his hand, humming a cheerful tune.

Two notorious confidence tricksters, observing the plump donkey and the merchant's relaxed demeanor, resolved to steal the animal. The first sharper whispered to his partner: 'Take the donkey by the pack-saddle and lead him down the side alley to the cattle market; I shall handle the halter and the merchant!'

While the second thief quietly slipped the halter off the donkey's ears and led the beast away, the first thief slipped the halter over his own neck and walked quietly behind the merchant in the donkey's footsteps!

After walking several streets, the thief suddenly stopped short, bracing his feet against the cobblestones. The merchant pulled on the rope, found it resisted, and turned around. To his utter amazement, he saw not his grey donkey, but a grown man wearing the halter around his neck, looking down with tearful remorse!

'By heavens!' gasped the merchant. 'Who are you, and where is my donkey?'

The trickster sighed deeply and wept: 'O generous master, know that I was born a human being, but because in my youth I spoke disrespectfully to my pious mother, she cursed me, and I was transformed into a donkey! For five years I have carried sacks of wheat and turned water-wheels to atone for my sin. Today, my mother’s heart softened, she prayed for my deliverance, and at this very hour my human form was restored to me!'

The merchant was struck with pious awe and horror. 'Forgive me, brother!' cried the merchant. 'May heaven witness that I did not know you were a human being when I loaded you with wheat!' He took the halter off the man's neck, gave him five dirhams for charity, and sent him away with blessings.

The next morning, the merchant went to the livestock market to purchase another beast. To his absolute bewilderment, he saw his exact same grey donkey standing in a dealer's pen! The merchant walked up, leaned close to the donkey's ear, and whispered sternly: 'Ah, you incorrigible rascal! You have gone and quarreled with your poor mother again, haven't you? By my honor, you may find another fool to buy you this time!'
moral: Greedy tricksters who scheme to swindle others often end up outwitting and exposing themselves.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Merchant and the Two Sharpers"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
